rows.evidence: Round-19 FAIL row L03-fig-bh-caption re-checked from scratch. Caption sentence 1, 'BH finds the last rank whose p-value lies on or under the rising line and rejects everything up to it, including any smaller p-value that sits above its own line': true in every state. BH rejects ranks 1 to k*; the set of carried ranks (k <= k* with p_k above k q/m) is non-empty only at q = 0.050 (k* = 5, carried rank 4; numeric/extra_checks.out, 38 of 39 values have none), so 'any' is vacuous elsewhere, and the sentence is true in all 39 states. Sentence 3, 'Holm's thresholds stay pinned near zero until the very last ranks': the Holm thresholds q/(m+1-k) for ranks 1 to 8 never exceed q/3 (0.0667 at q = 0.2) and only ranks 9 and 10 reach q/2 and q; drawn only when the Holm box is checked (default on). rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L04.html Proposition 1.3 and proof (lines 77-84); paragraph after it (line 86)
rows.evidence: unchanged since 3d65959 (git diff checked); round-19 evidence: Re-derived: by stationarity T Var(dbar) = T^-1 sum_{s,t} gamma(t - s) = sum_{|h| < T} (1 - |h|/T) gamma(h). The terms converge pointwise to gamma(h) and are dominated by |gamma(h)|, which is summable by (i), so T Var(dbar) -> sigma^2_LR. Under H0, DM = (sqrt T dbar/sigma_LR)(sigma_LR/sigma-hat_LR): the first factor -> N(0,1) by (ii); the second -> 1 in probability by (iii) and continuity of x -> sqrt(sigma^2_LR/x) at sigma^2_LR > 0; Slutsky gives the limit, so both the one-sided and two-sided tests have asymptotic level alpha. If mu > 0: DM = sqrt T mu/sigma-hat + sqrt T (dbar - mu)/sigma-hat, where the second term is O_p(1) and the first diverges. Assumptions complete and proof complete. Line 86: (iii) needs l to grow with T, and more slowly than T. That is consistent with Newey-West's Theorem 2 (m(T) -> inf with m(T)/T^(1/4) -> 0 under their conditions) and does not overstate a rate. || Round 8 (HEAD 8a7d2e6): git diff 9b6be31 HEAD -- course/modules/S/S7/L04.html has exactly five hunks (Remark 1.6, one clause; Remark 3.5, '\phi \gt 0'; Remark 4.3, the fan2015power span; Problem E4 solution with its snippet; the Remark 3.5 key-results row); a span-by-span comparison finds 53 of 54 claim/ref/grade spans identical (the 54th is the fan2015power span, re-checked in L04-cite-fan2015power). unchanged since 3d65959 (git diff checked); round-19 evidence: Re-checked from scratch (L04 line 100). Combination error e0 - lambda(e0 - e1); MSE = E[e0^2] - 2 lambda E[e0(e0 - e1)] + lambda^2 E[(e0 - e1)^2] (quadratic A - 2 lambda B + lambda^2 C, minimised at B/C with minimum A - B^2/C, checked numerically); lambda* = E[e0(e0 - e1)]/E[(e0 - e1)^2]; encompassing iff E[e0(e0 - e1)] = 0. The repaired example reads 'If both forecasts are unbiased, with mean squared error s^2 and error correlation rho < 1': unbiased means E e = 0, so E[e0 e1] = rho s^2, E[e0(e0 - e1)] = s^2(1 - rho) > 0, E[(e0 - e1)^2] = 2 s^2(1 - rho), lambda* = 1/2, MSE of the equal-weight combination = (2 s^2 + 2 rho s^2)/4 = s^2(1 + rho)/2 < s^2. Simulation (2,000,000 draws, s^2 = 1.69, rho = 0.3, verify8 inline numpy check): lambda* = 0.4995, E[e0(e0 - e1)] = 1.1832 against s^2(1 - rho) = 1.1830, combination MSE 1.0966 against 1.0985. A biased pair (means 1.0 and -0.8, correlation 0.3) gives E[e0(e0 - e1)] = 2.50 against the formula's 1.40, so the added hypothesis is necessary and sufficient for the stated formula. The conclusion 'a DM test would find nothing to choose between them, and the combination beats both' follows (equal MSE gives E d = 0). The two B spans of this remark are unchanged (harvey1998tests, bates1969combination; rows L04-cite-harvey1998tests, L04-cite-bates1969combination, L04-grade-remark1.6-sources).

rows.evidence: unchanged since 3d65959 (git diff checked); round-19 evidence: Re-derived at 7ff7507 from the printed paragraph; scripts remark35_limits.py (output remark35_limits.out) and signflip_check.py (outputs signflip_probe2.out, signflip_T2000.out). (1) Given the data, the reference law of T^(-1/2) sum_t eps_t d_t has variance T^(-1) sum_t d_t^2 (eps_t = +-1 i.i.d., mean 0, variance 1), so (H1) gives gamma(0). (2) The reference law is symmetric about 0, so its 95% quantile of |.| equals its 97.5% quantile of the signed sum; under (H2) both tend to the 0.975 quantile of N(0, gamma(0)). (3) Quantile identity checked numerically (remark35_limits.out section 1, g = 2.5): 95% quantile of |N(0,g)| = sqrt(g) z_0.975 = 3.0989751615, 97.5% quantile of N(0,g) = 3.0989751615 (equal); z_0.975 = 1.9599639845 (so 1.96 is the 97.5% quantile of N(0,1)). The literal misreading (97.5% quantile of |N(0,1)| = 2.2414027276) is not what the sentence now says. (4) (H3) gives T^(-1/2) sum d_t -> N(0, sigma2_LR); sigma2_LR/gamma(0) = (1+phi)/(1-phi) = 3 at phi = 0.5 and 1.857142857 at phi = 0.3 (remark35_limits.out section 2: direct sums over |h| <= 4000 agree with the closed form). (5) The limit: 2(1 - Phi(1.96 sqrt(gamma0/sigma2))) = 0.2577998945 at phi = 0.5 (page form 2(1 - Phi(1.132)) = 0.2576344344, rounds to 0.258) and 0.1503640418 at phi = 0.3 (page form 2(1 - Phi(1.438)) = 0.1504340541, rounds to 0.150) (remark35_limits.out section 3). Monte Carlo (signflip_check.py, Gaussian AR(1), phi = 0.5, unit innovations): at T = 2000, R = 3000, K = 499 random sign patterns, rejection rate 0.2523 (MC SE 0.0079) against the limit 0.2578 (signflip_T2000.out); conditional 95% quantile of T^(-1/2)|sum eps d| at T = 20000, K = 40000 is 2.292406 against 1.96 sqrt(T^(-1) sum d^2) = 2.285884 (within the quantile's Monte Carlo error, about 0.01). Advisory, not a failure: the last step (Slutsky with a continuous limit law at the cut-off) is used without being named; naming it would make the proof checkable at a glance.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html Lemma 2.3 (line 102) and its proof; card S7-c217
rows.evidence: unchanged since 3d65959 (git diff checked); round-19 evidence: Re-derived. (a) p_(k) <= kq/m iff at least k p-values are <= kq/m: if p_(k) <= kq/m then p_(1..k) are all <= kq/m, so N(k) >= k; if N(k) >= k then the k-th smallest is <= kq/m. Hence R = max{k : N(k) >= k}. (b) If R >= 1, a rejected H_i has p_i <= p_(R) <= Rq/m. Conversely, if p_i <= Rq/m but p_i = p_(j) with j > R, then p_(j) <= Rq/m <= jq/m, so N(j) >= j, contradicting the maximality of R; the zero case is handled (N(1) >= 1 forces R >= 1). (c) Raising a p-value can only lower each N(k), so the largest k with N(k) >= k cannot increase. Numerical spot check (scratch py/spotchecks_r12.py): for 2,000 random p-vectors (m = 10, q = 0.05, mixed scales) the BH rejection set equals {i : p_i <= R q/m} with R = max{k : N(k) >= k} (0 violations), and R does not increase when one randomly chosen p-value is raised (0 violations). Ties: the proof uses the k-th smallest p-value, so ties do not change the count.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html Proposition 5.3 (line 281) and its proof; card S7-c218
rows.evidence: unchanged since 3d65959 (git diff checked); round-19 evidence: Re-derived for rho in [0,1). Given z_i = t, the joint Gaussian (W, z_i) gives W | z_i = t ~ N(sqrt(rho)(t - mu_i), 1 - rho), stochastically increasing in t for rho >= 0 (the constant case rho = 0 is trivially monotone). The other coordinates are z_j = sqrt(rho) W + sqrt(1-rho) eps_j + mu_j with eps_j independent of (W, z_i), so P(z in D' | z_i = t) = E[g(W) | z_i = t], g non-increasing for a decreasing D' (translating all z_j by a common amount). Hence t -> P(z in D' | z_i = t) is non-increasing, which is PRDS (Definition 5.1) on every subset. Numerical spot check (scratch py/spotchecks_r12.py, Monte Carlo 600,000 draws, rho = 0.5, m = 3, D = {p_2 >= 1/2, p_3 >= 1/2}, an increasing set in p-space): P(D | z_1 near t) falls from 0.556 at t = -1 to 0.033 at t = 2 (non-increasing in t), and P(D | p_1 near u) rises from 0.054 at u = 0.05 to 0.708 at u = 0.95 (non-decreasing in u): the PRDS inequality holds in the numerical check. (An earlier attempt used the z-increasing set {z_2 > 0, z_3 > 0}; that set is not an increasing set of p-values, so it was discarded.)

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L04.html line 365 (section 6, the T span: 'Step 2 of Definition 4.1 subtracts each strategy's own sample mean ... never more')
rows.evidence: unchanged since 3d65959 (git diff checked); round-19 evidence: Re-derived from Definition 4.1 (L04.html lines 268–275: V_K = max_k sqrt(T) dbar_k; V*_{K,j} = max_k sqrt(T)(dbar*_{k,j} - dbar_k) with one index sequence per draw shared by all strategies; p-hat = mean_j 1{V*_{K,j} >= V_K}). (a) Adding any strategy adds one term to each maximum: V*_{K+1,j} = max(V*_{K,j}, term_j) >= V*_{K,j} for every draw j. (b) If its statistic s = sqrt(T) dbar_{K+1} is not the largest (s <= V_K), then V_{K+1} = V_K. (c) Hence with the same draws p-hat can only rise, and rejection at alpha (p-hat <= alpha) can only be lost. Numerical check of (a)–(c) with the Definition 4.1 procedure, seed 20261020, 300 trials, T = 120, B = 400, K from 2 to 7 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify22h-L03-L04/derive/rc_pathwise_check.py, output /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify22h-L03-L04/derive/rc_pathwise_check.out): non-largest additions 210: V_K unchanged in 210 of 210; V*_(K+1,j) >= V*_(K,j) for every draw in all 300 trials (0 violations); p-hat fell in 0 of 210.
